spec.title: CBMC 6.11.0's source times Runtime Post-process inside Runtime Solver
spec.description: Network fetch: downloads two source files of CBMC at the tag cbmc-6.11.0 from raw.githubusercontent.com (goto-checker/bmc_util.cpp and solvers/prop/prop_conv_solver.cpp) and prints the code that times JBMC's solver calls. Phase 1a of llm-dlc/loops/engine-priorities.md reads JBMC's phases per solver call, on the claim that run_property_decider's 'Runtime Solver' times the whole call, and that prop_conv_solvert::dec_solve, inside it, runs finish_eager_conversion and reports it as 'Runtime Post-process'. lib/src/phases.rs now counts the post-processing under encoding alone and the rest of the call under solving. Real JBMC 6.11.0 runs (lib/tests/fixtures/jbmc-phases/) already show the nesting from their message times; the brief asks for the source to be checked too, and agents fetch from the network only inside a job.
spec.expected: Both files download; bmc_util.cpp's run_property_decider takes the time around property_decider.solve() and prints it as 'Runtime Solver'; prop_conv_solver.cpp's dec_solve calls finish_eager_conversion() and prints its time as 'Runtime Post-process' before calling the SAT solver. The step exits 0 when all three strings are found.

steps.name: fetch and show CBMC 6.11.0's solver timers
steps.run: set -euo pipefail; base=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/diffblue/cbmc/cbmc-6.11.0/src; d=$(mktemp -d); curl -fsSL "$base/goto-checker/bmc_util.cpp" -o "$d/bmc_util.cpp"; curl -fsSL "$base/solvers/prop/prop_conv_solver.cpp" -o "$d/prop_conv_solver.cpp"; sha256sum "$d"/*.cpp; echo "== bmc_util.cpp: run_property_decider"; grep -n -A45 "^decision_proceduret::resultt run_property_decider" "$d/bmc_util.cpp" | head -70; echo "== prop_conv_solver.cpp: dec_solve"; grep -n -A40 "prop_conv_solvert::dec_solve" "$d/prop_conv_solver.cpp" | head -60; grep -q "Runtime Solver" "$d/bmc_util.cpp"; grep -q "Runtime Post-process" "$d/prop_conv_solver.cpp"; grep -q "finish_eager_conversion" "$d/prop_conv_solver.cpp"; rm -rf "$d"
